step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram depicts Triboo's e-commerce platform based on Magento. Traffic starts at Route 53, which routes external domains and internal requests to WAF for anti-DDoS and bot protection. Screened traffic moves to CloudFront, which uses behaviors to serve static content directly from S3 or forward dynamic requests to a custom Pass Secure Load Balancer running on EC2. The load balancer routes backend requests into an EKS Kubernetes cluster. EKS interacts with ElasticSearch for search indexing, ElastiCache for session and app caching, a dedicated EC2 NFS server for shared storage, Aurora MySQL for relational e-commerce transactions, and S3 for static assets and logs. Additional standalone services include a VPN entry point for administration, Lambda for monitoring and alerting, RedShift for business intelligence, and an EC2 instance acting as a mail server.

nodes.name: EKS Cluster

nodes.name: ElasticSearch
nodes.notes: Search indexing engine integrated with EKS.

nodes.name: ElastiCache
nodes.notes: In-memory caching layer for application cache and user sessions.

nodes.name: EC2 NFS Server

nodes.name: S3 Bucket

nodes.name: VPC VPN
nodes.notes: IPsec VPN entry point for managing all AWS infrastructure services.

nodes.name: Lambda
nodes.notes: Serverless compute used for system configuration, monitoring, and alerting.

edges.notes: Route 53 routes incoming web traffic into WAF.
WAF passes inspected and filtered web requests to CloudFront.
CloudFront routes static asset requests directly to S3.
CloudFront forwards dynamic requests to Pass Secure LB on EC2.
EC2 load balancer directs backend application traffic to EKS.
EKS queries ElasticSearch for product search indexing.
EKS manages user sessions and cache through ElastiCache.
EKS mounts and accesses shared files on the custom EC2 NFS server.
EKS executes transactional queries on the Aurora MySQL database.
EKS reads and writes static media elements and log files to S3.
